A maintainer reading only the YAML (not the milestone doc) would understand why each guard exists.

must_fix.description: Both vendor jobs' 'Bench regression gate' step runs `cargo test --release -p axc-driver --test bench_regression -- --nocapture` but neither job's env: block (job-level or step-level) ever sets AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION="1". crates/axc-driver/tests/bench_regression.rs:209-212 short-circuits (prints 'skipping bench regression' and returns Ok) whenever that var isn't exactly "1". Compare against the existing, working ci.yml `bench-regression` job (ci.yml:61 and :86), which DOES set AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION: "1" at job level -- that's the only reason it actually gates today. As merged, once an AMD/Intel runner activates, the vendor 'Bench regression gate' step will run, print the skip message, and exit 0 EVERY time, regardless of whether baselines.json has a key for that machine or whether a real regression occurred. This silently defeats one of the three §4.1 per-PR deliverables and directly contradicts the milestone's own no-vacuous-pass ethos (the same discipline AT-3033 exists to enforce for the YAML parser). Spec §4.1 explicitly requires 'AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION=1' in the vendor job's bench-regression step; the shipped YAML omits it.
must_fix.why_untested: AT-3028 (GPU-test step parity) only checks AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS / VK_DRIVER_FILES on the ignored-suite step. AT-3031 (vendor-independence linkage) diffs only the `run:` command string between the Lavapipe and vendor bench-regression steps ('byte-identical modulo the ICD env') -- it never inspects the enclosing env: block, so two jobs with an identical command but a missing enabling var pass AT-3031 vacuously. No AT in the 3019..3035 range asserts AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION is present on the vendor bench-regression step.
must_fix.suggested_fix: Add `AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION: "1"` to the job-level env: block of both amd-gpu and intel-gpu in cross-vendor-ci.yml (alongside AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS/AXC_REQUIRE_SPIRV_VAL). Recommend also tightening AT-3031 (or adding a new AT) to assert the bench-regression step's effective env includes AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION="1" on every job that runs the `--test bench_regression` command, so this class of bug can't recur.

minor_issues.description: AT-3031's 'vendor-independence linkage' framing ('byte-identical modulo the ICD env') is true only of the run: step text; it doesn't cover job env:, which is exactly where the AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION gap above lives. Worth broadening the assertion's scope or its doc comment to be explicit that it only proves command parity, not full environment parity.

summary: The workflow YAML, EB1_RUNNER_SETUP.md, and eb1_workflow_ci.rs are all high quality, well-documented, and faithful to the r2 spec in every structural/security dimension the 17 ATs cover (activation gating, fork guard, permissions, timeouts, pull_request_target absence, Mesa honesty, docs completeness, ROADMAP/UPSTREAM_PR_PLAN edits). However, direct inspection found a concrete functional bug that slipped past the Coder, QA, and all 17 ATs: cross-vendor-ci.yml's amd-gpu/intel-gpu jobs never set AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION="1", so their 'Bench regression gate' step will silently no-op (short-circuit and pass) on real hardware, contradicting spec §4.1 and the milestone's own anti-vacuous-pass principle. This is a small, precise, one-line-per-job fix, but it is spec non-compliance in a load-bearing deliverable, so verdict is NEEDS_REVISION rather than APPROVE.

observed: FIX PRESENT: cross-vendor-ci.yml now sets AXC_ENABLE_BENCH_REGRESSION: "1" at JOB level on BOTH vendor jobs — amd-gpu (line 49) and intel-gpu (line 96), alongside AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS/AXC_REQUIRE_SPIRV_VAL exactly as suggested. Each carries an explanatory comment tying it to bench_regression.rs:209 and mirroring ci.yml:61.
